tractatione vtendum, quę in nunciatoriis

liaribus: multæ ac variæ in iis, quas ad At-
ticum Cicero scripsit, hominem doctum
& amicum intimum: & tempore scripsit
Reipublicæ admodum periculoso. Vt lib.
1. epist.15. vbi rectè Cicero de adulterio a-
git cuiusdam Cai cum Luculli vxore, &
illum quidem Paridem, hunc Menelaum
vocat: & de togula picta Pompeij: & pi-
scatoribus, Lucullo, Hortensio, L. Philip-
po, qui abiecta Reipublicæ cura, de pisci-
nis suis foliciti erant. lib.2. epist.9. vbi de
Clodio, Pompeio, Reipublicę etiam statu
obscurè

page.notes: Left margin notes: "Collocatio & tractatio sententiarum." (beside "ac perspicuum nihil reperiri solet") and "Materiæ ænigmaticarum epistolarum." (beside "Sunt autem materię"). Some letters are faint at the gutter; "necefsitas" and "scripsit" were read from the scan with confidence but the gutter-side words are less clear. The line "obscurè" is set right-aligned at the foot of the page and is the last printed line, not a catchword.
